I would buy the 9Barista Mk.2 for one or two straight espressos when counter space or access to electricity is genuinely constrained. It is a precisely engineered brewer, not a small all-purpose espresso station.
One straight-espresso drinker who values repeatability more than pressure or temperature profiling
9Barista Espresso Machine Mk.2 stovetop espresso brewer

The current US Steel Duo PID is a persuasive choice for someone who wants a 58 mm machine, adjustable brew temperature, volumetric buttons, and espresso and steam at the same time without waiting for traditional boilers.
A milk-drink household that wants to extract and steam at the same time from a compact 58 mm machine
Black Ascaso Steel Duo PID espresso machine with walnut controls

The Steel Uno PID makes sense when you want Ascaso’s 58 mm group, adjustable temperature, programmable pre-infusion, volumetric buttons, gauge, and quick on-demand heating, but milk is occasional and a 1050 W single circuit suits the kitchen better than the Duo.
An espresso-first household that wants 58 mm accessories, PID control, a gauge, and programmable pre-infusion
Black Ascaso Steel Uno PID espresso machine with walnut controls

The BZ09 is a solid narrow single boiler whose cartridge-heated BZ group gives it more identity than its sparse control panel suggests. Buy it when local Bezzera support is strong and manual temperature routine is part of the appeal.
Espresso-first buyer who wants a compact 58 mm traditional machine
Bezzera BZ09 stainless steel espresso machine viewed from the front

The BZ10 turns a narrow counter slot into a capable espresso-and-steam station. Its cartridge-heated group and 1.5 L heat exchanger support a quick manual bar rhythm, but temperature remains an inferred routine rather than a displayed recipe setting.
Milk-drink household that needs espresso and steam at the same time
Bezzera BZ10 stainless steel heat-exchanger espresso machine viewed from the front

The BZ13 PID is a strong match for a milk-drink household that wants a narrow traditional machine, quicker group readiness than a large E61, and either manual PM control or the DE model’s volumetric buttons.
Milk-drink households that want HX steam and simultaneous brewing in a narrow body
Bezzera BZ13 PID espresso machine in polished stainless steel
The Duo MN is for a buyer who wants to lift an E61 lever but does not want an old-fashioned control system.
An E61 buyer who wants dual-boiler separation and a genuinely useful touchscreen
Bezzera Duo MN dual-boiler espresso machine with E61 group and touchscreen
The Bezzera Hobby 01 makes a convincing case at the $799 US price checked September 17, 2026: commercial-size coffee hardware, a three-liter tank and unusually energetic steam in a narrow body.
One or two daily drinks from a narrow, substantial machine
Bezzera Hobby 01 compact espresso machine in stainless steel
Mitica Top PID is compelling when a rotary pump, E61 lever, plumbing flexibility and simultaneous milk service are the goal.
Household making repeated espresso and milk drinks
Bezzera Mitica Top PID polished stainless heat-exchanger espresso machine
Choose the Strega when the declining-pressure character and physical ritual of a spring lever are the point, while a service boiler and pump-assisted fill keep milk drinks practical.
Buyer specifically seeking a spring-driven declining pressure profile
Bezzera Strega spring-lever espresso machine in polished stainless steel
Choose the Unica PID when straight espresso, a traditional lever group, compact width, and visible temperature selection matter more than rapid milk-drink service.
Espresso-first household making occasional milk drinks
Bezzera Unica PID stainless single-boiler espresso machine
Choose the Bosch 300 Series when easy black coffee and in-cup milk frothing matter more than a broad drink library or app control.
Household wanting simple bean-to-cup coffee below four-figure list price
Bosch 300 Series VeroCafe TIU20307 fully automatic espresso machine
Choose the Bosch 500 Series when the 300 feels too limited but the 800’s screen, profiles, app, and 35-drink library are unnecessary.
Household making several coffee and milk recipes
Bosch 500 Series VeroCafe TPU40109 fully automatic espresso machine
Choose the Bosch 800 Series when several people will genuinely use its 35 drinks, ten profiles, five-inch display, Home Connect controls, and integrated milk workflow.
Several users with different saved drinks
Bosch 800 Series VeroCafe TPU60309 connected fully automatic espresso machine
I would choose the Bambino Plus for a household making lattes and cappuccinos most days. Its quick-start heater and automatic milk remove two chores, but you still grind, dose and tamp.
A household that wants repeatable milk drinks with less milk-steaming practice
Breville Bambino Plus espresso machine

The Barista Express remains a coherent first espresso station for someone who wants the grinder and machine in one familiar package. Its pressure gauge, manual wand and current single-wall baskets leave real room to learn.
A first-time owner who wants one coordinated coffee station and is willing to learn manual espresso
Breville Barista Express BES870XL espresso machine with integrated grinder

The Barista Express Impress is the strongest Breville choice when inconsistent dosing, crooked tamping and loose grounds make several household users avoid espresso. Its feedback loop learns from the previous dose and the lever applies a repeatable tamp.
Several household users who need a repeatable dose and level tamp without loose-ground mess
Breville Barista Express Impress BES876 with assisted tamp lever
The Barista Pro is the Breville integrated model I would choose when speed, a shot timer and more usable grind adjustment matter every morning.
Someone who wants an integrated grinder but dislikes the Express warm-up and analog-only workflow
Breville Barista Pro BES878 espresso machine with integrated grinder and LCD

The Barista Touch is a strong bridge between manual espresso and one-touch convenience. Its touchscreen, quick ThermoJet heater and automatic milk system make lattes approachable, but it still asks you to dose, distribute, tamp, move and clean a 54 mm portafilter.
A latte or cappuccino household that wants automatic milk and touchscreen guidance
Breville Barista Touch BES880 espresso machine with touchscreen and integrated grinder
Choose the Barista Touch Impress when several users want touchscreen guidance, assisted dosing and tamping, and automatic milk while keeping a real portafilter workflow.

segments.source: Choose the Dynamic Duo when the bundle price is competitive and a single purchase for a capable 58 mm dual boiler plus a usable grinder matters. The BES920 is the star: independent boilers, PID, programmable preinfusion, front filling, and simultaneous steam remain compelling.
Buyer wanting a complete 58 mm dual-boiler setup in one order
Breville Dynamic Duo BEP920 dual boiler espresso machine and Smart Grinder Pro bundle
Choose the original Oracle BES980 when its 58 mm automated grind, dose and tamp, independent boilers, and automatic milk are worth prioritizing over a modern touchscreen or faster cold start.
Milk-drink household wanting simultaneous assisted preparation
Breville Oracle BES980 assisted dual-boiler espresso machine with integrated grinder

Choose the Oracle Jet when you want automated 58 mm grind, dose and tamp, active Barista Guidance, rapid ThermoJet startup, Auto MilQ, a modern touchscreen, and update capability without moving to a sealed brew unit.
Household wanting highly guided 58 mm espresso
Breville Oracle Jet BES985 premium guided espresso machine in brushed stainless steel
The Oracle Touch remains a rare and appealing hybrid: it grinds, doses and tamps into a 58 mm portafilter, then runs espresso and automatic milk on a dual-boiler platform.
A buyer who specifically wants automatic grind, dose and tamp with a removable 58 mm portafilter
Breville Oracle Touch BES990 dual-boiler espresso machine with touchscreen and grinder

The Breville Dual Boiler offers the controls that matter to an ambitious home barista: separate brew and steam boilers, a heated group, adjustable temperature and pre-infusion, a 58 mm portafilter and simultaneous brewing and steaming.
An espresso enthusiast who already owns, or has budgeted for, a capable separate grinder
Breville Dual Boiler BES920XL espresso machine with two boilers and pressure gauge

Choose the Robot Barista when you want quiet, direct pressure control in a compact mechanical tool and already accept the separate grinder and kettle. Skip it when milk drinks, effortless heat management, or push-button repeatability matter more than tactile espresso.
Straight-espresso drinker who enjoys controlling pressure by hand
Retro green Cafelat Robot Barista manual lever espresso maker
Choose the CREM ONE 1B PID Dual when a narrow E61 heat exchanger, simultaneous brewing and steaming, PID interface, and tank-to-mains flexibility match the kitchen.
Milk-drink household wanting a narrow traditional E61 machine
CREM ONE HX PID espresso machine in polished stainless steel
Choose the original Dalla Corte Mina when programmable flow, a compact multiboiler chassis, powerful steam, and fixed-water installation belong in a permanent enthusiast station.
Advanced espresso buyer who wants direct and saved flow profiles
White Dalla Corte Mina Barista espresso machine shown as the current evolution of Mina

The EC685 remains a defensible small-kitchen starter when it is substantially cheaper than newer compact machines. Its stock pressurized workflow is forgiving, its body is genuinely narrow and its settings are more useful than the three-button panel suggests.
A genuinely narrow counter where most espresso machines will not fit
De'Longhi Dedica EC685 compact espresso machine

Choose the ECP3420 when the budget is tight, pressurized baskets and pre-ground coffee provide a practical starting point, and one or two milk drinks are enough. Do not mistake the 15-bar label for advanced control or expect a small single-heater machine to serve a queue quickly.

De'Longhi Eletta Explore fully automatic espresso machine
